Regenerated 2026-09-26 on branch feat/phase10-14-complete. Previous stored value recall@10 0.825 / mrr 0.6322 was written at d80ffb6, where the same command measures 0.850.

The gate was failing before this regeneration, and the cause was bisected rather than assumed. Measured by checking out each corpus and running the eval against it (the eval is hermetic: it materialises git-tracked files into a temp dir and uses a temp DB, so AI_DB_PATH is inert for it):
  corpus @ d80ffb6, where 0.825 was recorded   recall@10 0.850  pass
  corpus @ e8ed971 (pre-session HEAD)         recall@10 0.725  fail by 0.100
  current code on that same e8ed971 corpus     recall@10 0.725, mrr 0.4336
  corpus @ d2222f7 (pre-commit)                recall@10 0.725
  corpus @ HEAD (9e3c836, committed)           recall@10 0.825  <- this file

Two corrections to the story I told earlier, both found by re-measuring:
1. The 'current code + this session's files = 0.700' figure I quoted was taken on a working tree where the new files were still UNTRACKED. The eval indexes git-tracked files only, so it was measuring a smaller corpus than the committed one -- not a comparable number. Measured on the committed tree it is 0.825.
2. The commit did not cost recall; it recovered 4 queries (0.725 -> 0.825) and lost none: 'delete file cascade remove symbols annotations', 'semantic cache lookup by file hash', 'todo fixme hack annotations extraction', 'which files should be indexed node_modules venv rules'.

Actual cause of the 0.850 -> 0.825 slide: one query, 'extract symbols from python ast' (expects ai_db/parser/ts_graph.py::extract_graph), went 1.00 -> 0.00. Test files crowd out the source they test, because they are named after the functions they exercise. For that query the top 9 are 6 tests/ files (tests/test_parser.py x3, tests/test_ts_graph.py, tests/test_phase14.py) and only 3 ai_db/parser files, and ts_graph.py lands at rank 10-11. tests/ grew through Phase 10-15, so this is drift from corpus composition, not a code regression: the current code reproduces the old code's numbers exactly on an unchanged corpus (row 3 above).

eval/results/ is now in .aidbignore so generated benchmark artifacts stay out of the search space -- before that, eval/results/*.json was ranking 3rd and 4th for this very query. That fix is real; it is not what recovers the 0.850.

No golden entry has been edited: eval/golden/ai_db.jsonl has not changed since d80ffb6. The open question this exposes is a design one, not a bug: should a code-QA index rank tests/ equally with source? Excluding tests/ from the eval corpus, or down-weighting test files, is the obvious lever to test next.
